intro: Spektt is built for creatives — photographers, videographers, 3D animators, sound engineers, and digital artists — to share real work and compete fairly. These guidelines exist so the platform stays worth posting to.
appliesTo: They apply everywhere on Spektt: uploads, Spotlights, comments, captions, profiles, Cluster posts, Showdown entries, and direct messages.
ageNote: You must be 16 or older to use Spektt. Direct messaging and Showdown entry are 18+.

s1.heading: 1. Post work that is yours
s1.body: Only post content you created, or content you have the rights to post.
items: Reposting another creative's work as your own will get it removed.
Using copyrighted material without permission is not allowed.
If your work was posted by someone else without permission, email legal@spektt.com with the details and we will act.
For a plagiarised Showdown entry, report the entry with "Intellectual Property" and include a link to the original — or email showdowns@spektt.com directly.

s2.heading: 2. Treat people as people
s2.body: No harassment, bullying, threats, or repeated unwanted contact. No hate speech — content that promotes hatred based on race, religion, gender, or any other identity. No content targeting someone's ethnicity, religion, gender, or background.
s2.blocking: Blocking is always available: go to the profile, open the three-dot menu, and choose Block. A blocked person cannot see your content, comment on your posts, or message you.

s3.heading: 3. Keep it safe
items: Content that endangers or exploits minors, in any form
Content that promotes or glorifies self-harm or suicide
Real violence, gore, or disturbing imagery
Explicit nudity or sexual material
Promotion of illegal goods or services
s3.priority: Child safety and self-harm reports are treated as critical and reviewed first.
s3.support: If you are struggling, please reach out to a local crisis line. We would rather you talk to someone than post about it.

s4.heading: 4. Be who you say you are
s4.intro: One real person, one real account.
items: No impersonating another person, creative, or brand
No accounts that do not represent a real person
No accounts under the minimum age
If your account is compromised, reset your password immediately and contact support@spektt.com

s5.heading: 5. Do not game the system
s5.intro: Spektt runs competitions with real prizes. Fairness is the product.
items: No vote manipulation, vote buying, or coordinated voting rings
No duplicate or multi-account entries
No advertising prizes you will not award
No rigged judging
No exploiting a bug for advantage — report it instead
s5.note: Showdown integrity issues can be reported directly on the Showdown.

s6.heading: 6. No spam
s6.body: No repetitive posting, unsolicited promotion, link drops, fake giveaways, or artificially inflated engagement.

s7.heading: 7. Do not spread harmful false information
s7.body: Misinformation that could cause real-world harm will be removed.

s8.heading: 8. Clusters have rules too
s8.intro: Clusters are community spaces. Every Cluster on Spektt carries these rules, and a Cluster admin can add rules on top but can never remove or override them:
tableRows: No harassment, hate speech, or personal attacks toward any member
Posts must relate to the Cluster's creative focus
No repetitive posts, unsolicited promotion, or link drops
Explicit or adult content isn't allowed on Spektt
Clusters are community spaces — all competitions with prize money are hosted exclusively in Showdowns
Only share content you created or have the rights to
Content or comments targeting ethnicity, religion, gender, or background will not be tolerated
Our platform-wide rules always apply inside every Cluster
s8.screening: Cluster names and descriptions are screened. Names that promote hate, extremism, illegal activity, sexual exploitation of minors, or violence are blocked at creation. Names using protected brands require verification.
s8.moderators: Cluster admins can appoint moderators once the Cluster is large enough. Moderators accept a separate set of moderator guidelines before they can act, and their powers are limited — a moderator cannot delete content that does not break the rules.

s9.heading: 9. How reporting works
s9.intro: Tap the three-dot menu on any post, comment, Showdown, Showdown entry, or profile and select Report, then choose the reason that fits best. Reports are reviewed by real people, not only by automated systems.
s9.tableIntro: How quickly we review, by severity:
tableRows: Hate speech, harassment, violence, nudity, impersonation, illegal goods, rigged judging
Copyright, false information, fake accounts, fake contests
s9.note: Reporting someone does not tell them you reported them.

s10.heading: 10. What happens when a rule is broken
s10.intro: Consequences scale with severity and history. We do not use a fixed strike count — serious violations skip straight to suspension.
items: Content removal — the post, comment, or entry comes down.

Warning — a formal warning you receive in the app and as a push notification. Warnings are recorded on your account and cannot be turned off in notification settings, because a warning you never see cannot change anything.
Suspension — 7 days, 14 days, 30 days, or permanent. A timed suspension lifts automatically when it expires. While suspended you cannot use the app.
Permanent ban — for the most serious violations, or repeated ones.
s10.clusterNote: Separately, a Cluster admin or moderator can remove your post from their Cluster or remove you from that Cluster, without affecting your Spektt account.

s11.heading: 11. Appealing
s11.intro: If your account is suspended you will see a screen explaining why, and you can appeal from that screen.
items: Up to 2 appeals per suspension. The second only unlocks if the first is declined.
An appeal must be between 50 and 1,000 characters — enough to actually explain.
A new suspension resets the count.
You cannot appeal while an appeal is already under review.
s11.contact: You can also email support@spektt.com with your username.

s12.heading: 12. Contact
s12.closing: These guidelines work alongside our Terms and Conditions. Where the Terms are the agreement, these guidelines are how we apply it.
